reuse.why: Builds on the existing getScheduledAmount for the range rule and routes all five server copies through it, but re-implements the 7.5% tolerance instead of calling the existing getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.

duplication.why: Removes the four inline midpoint copies and the template copy; the tolerance formula duplicates getApproxNumberThreshold, and schedule-template keeps an op dispatch that duplicates the helper's own handling.

placement.why: The expected-amount rule sits in shared/schedules.ts beside getScheduledAmount, consumed by server, forecast, API model and preview.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the amount rule, its callers, the API field and tests.

maintainability.why: The rule is now split over two exported functions (getScheduledAmount for ranges, getExpectedScheduleAmount adding approximate), client code still calls only the former so it ignores the approximate rule, and the op is an untyped optional string.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount in shared/schedules.ts computes Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) instead of using getApproxNumberThreshold (shared/rules.ts); schedule-template.ts decides op === 'isbetween' || 'isapprox' itself before calling the helper.

disguised_duplication.where: The tolerance formula is copied openly; the old midpoint copies were removed rather than reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: A wrapper getExpectedScheduleAmount(amount, op) with an isapprox special case layered over getScheduledAmount; schedule-template.ts keeps its own op dispatch around the call (desktop-client callers keep using getScheduledAmount without the op).
